label: Ubiquiti UniFi Mobile Router (UMR)
description: UniFi Mobile Router: 2x 1G RJ45, LTE Cat 4 (150/50 Mbps), WiFi 4, PoE+ input with 10 W PoE passthrough, DIN/wall mount.
notes: Vendor figures: **(2) GbE RJ45 ports**, **LTE Cat 4** (150 Mbps down / 50 Mbps up), WiFi 4 1x1, 9 W, PoE+ (48-54 V) or USB-C or 4-pin ATX DC. The PoE row is the interesting one: **(1) PoE input and (1) PoE output, max 10 W, which requires a PoE+ switch** - so it can be powered by the switch it sits on *and* pass power through to one downstream device, but only when the upstream is PoE+ rather than plain 802.3af. **Cited 2026-11-19.** Port row, 9 W draw and the PoE classes: https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/integrations/umr-us (200, 708,698 B) prints "Networking Interface (2) GbE RJ45 ports, LTE Cat 4 radio, WiFi 4", "PoE Interface (1) PoE input / (1) PoE output (Max. 10W, requires PoE+ switch)", "Max. Power Consumption 9W" and "Power Method PoE+ (48-54V DC)". Datasheet https://dl.ui.com/ds/umr_ds.pdf (200, application/pdf, 597,924 B, two pages, text layer) prints the same census as "(2) GbE RJ45 ports" and "(1) PoE in / (1) PoE output*" with "*Requires a PoE+ switch" - but no output wattage, so the 10 W budget is a tech-spec-only figure. The store page https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/umr-us (307 to its collection URL, 200 there at 585,616 B) corroborates it in prose: "PoE+ input required for PoE passthrough." The two documents disagree on the chassis - datasheet 220.6 x 89.8 x 28.8 mm and 252/298 g against tech-spec 190 x 89.8 x 28.8 mm and 257/303 g - while the ports, the 150 Mbps WiFi 4 rate and the 9 W draw are identical on both, and those are what the row models. Neither surface publishes *which* RJ45 is the input, only that there is one of each, so rj45-1 sinks (9 W) and rj45-2 sources (PoE+), the same convention as devices/zyxel/gs1900-24ep.json. The -us suffix is required on both hosts: store /products/umr is 404 and techspecs .../integrations/umr lands on the 609,911-byte front page. **The cellular port (added 2026-11-19).** Both vendor surfaces name an *LTE Cat 4 radio*, and the datasheet prints its rate - `https://dl.ui.com/ds/umr_ds.pdf` (200, application/pdf, 597,924 B, 2 pp, text layer) page 2: "LTE throughput speed* Download 150 Mbps / Upload 50 Mbps"; the tech-spec page prints the same row as "LTE Throughput Speed Download 150 Mbps / Upload 50 Mbps" beside "LTE Cat 4 radio". Until this pass the row modelled the two copper ports and the WiFi 4 radio only, so the radio the product is named for had no interface at all and the cellular WAN this device exists to provide could not be cabled - the #129 shape, one level up from a missing medium. `wwan0` is now `150M`, the published **download** figure, the convention `udr-5g-max` (5G NSA downlink) and `u5g-max` already use; the 50 Mbps uplink is recorded here rather than in a field because the schema carries one rate per port. The engine resolves the `wwan0` spelling to the cellular cage, so the row offers LTE and no Wi-Fi band. **The 10 W is now on the socket (2026-11-21).** The row carried `poeOut: true`, the bare direction bit, which `Device.poeDraw()` reads as 1 W and `pseDraw()` sums against this 10 W budget - so a powered device on the one PSE port could never be billed above 1 W and the budget could not bind. `poeOut: 10` is the figure Ubiquiti prints for that socket: "(1) PoE output (Max. 10W, requires PoE+ switch)" (techspecs, 200, 708,698 B measured today). The `poeOutClass` stays PoE+ because that is the upstream feed the port requires; the 10 W ceiling is a passthrough cap, not the class ceiling, so the two fields deliberately disagree. Trap recorded: /unifi/cloud-gateways/umr and /umr-industrial 307 to / - the live pages are under /unifi/integrations/ with the -us suffix.

poe.note: (1) PoE output, max 10 W, and it requires a PoE+ switch upstream - so the passthrough is bounded at 10 W on the one PSE port (rj45-2). The 10 W is printed only by the tech-spec page; the datasheet states the port count and the PoE+ upstream requirement but no output wattage.
